# Mūlapariyāya Sutta (MN 1 (PTS MN i 1))

**ID:** MN 1 (PTS MN i 1)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Mūlapariyāya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mūlapariyāya Sutta* ("The Root of All Things" or "The Discourse on the Root of Existence") is the opening discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* (MN 1) [Bodhi 1980]. In this foundational text, the Buddha investigates the cognitive processes through which the notion of a permanent self emerges from perception, expounding how craving, conceit, and views govern distortion [Bodhi 2003; Bodhi 1980]. The discourse examines a sequence of phenomena extending from the physical elements (such as earth, *pathavī*) to cosmological planes and ultimate categories; an uninstructed person perceives a phenomenon and "conceives" (*maññati*) it in terms of selfhood—conceiving himself as it, in it, apart from it, or conceiving it as "mine" [Buddhist Philosophy 2012a; Bodhi 2003; Bodhi 1980]. In contrast, disciples in higher training and arahants experience the same range of phenomena directly without conceptual proliferation or attachment [Bodhi 2003].

Bhikkhu Bodhi published a comprehensive study and translation of the sutta along with its commentarial apparatus under the title *The Discourse on the Root of Existence* [Bodhi 1980; Bodhi 2003].

Curated parallels recorded for the sutta include Chinese translations preserved in the *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 106), the *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 44.6), and the individual translation *Lèxiǎng jīng* (樂想經, T 56); the sutta is also cited in the Theravāda *Kathāvatthu* (Kv 9.2, *Amatārammaṇakathā*).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: EA 44.6 法之本
- Resembling parallels: MA 106 想; T 56 樂想
- Mentioned in: Kv 9.2 Amatārammaṇakathā

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 1980] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Discourse on the Root of Existence: The Mūlapariyāya Sutta and its Commentarial Exegesis (1980) — Significance and position of MN 1, theme of conceiving and egocentric orientation, and details of commentary and subcommentary.
- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikāya (2003) — Analysis of the fourfold pattern of conceiving (maññanā) and relation to sense bases and identity view.
- [Buddhist Philosophy 2012a] Proceedings of the 2nd IABU Conference: Buddhist Philosophy and Meditation Practice (2012) — Quotes the opening earth-conceiving formula of MN 1 and its translation.
- [Ñāṇamoli and Bodhi 1995] Bhikkhu Ñāṇamoli and Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Middle Length Discourses of the Buddha (1995) — Bibliographic record of the translation of MN 1 and its commentary.
